fixtures.source: Lumina sensor array logged 18 false positives on 2039-11-04 when ambient dust rose above 40 μg/m³. Cross-referencing proved that a laser calibration drift of 2.1 mm caused 12 of the false positives. The evidence does not show what caused the remaining 6 false positives. During the spike, internal temperatures increased from 28°C to 34°C. The evidence neither establishes the temperature increase as the cause of the remaining 6 nor excludes it. Signal reflection was ruled out as a cause.

semantic_claims.proposition: Laser calibration drift of 2.1 mm caused 12 of the false positives.
The cause for the remaining 6 false positives is not established by the evidence.
The internal temperature increase is neither proven nor excluded as the cause of the remaining 6 false positives.
Signal reflection was ruled out as a cause of the false positives.
The Lumina sensor array logged 18 false positives on 2039-11-04 when ambient dust rose above 40 μg/m³.
During the spike, internal temperatures increased from 28°C to 34°C.

fixtures.source: At Aethel Facility, shift supervisors must lock bay `B-42` when radiation exceeds 15 mSv/h. fixtures.source: Notice for payload engineers. Since 2041-02-18, Valerius firmware 4.1.9 displays `overpressure` when the auxiliary tank exceeds 450 kPa. The `overpressure` state means the panel freezes the last validated flow rate. The display of `overpressure` does not mean the main valve has failed. If `overpressure` persists for 5 minutes, engineers should inspect the relief valve. When bypass `BYP-11` is active, engineers must not reset the module. A reset clears the display but does not vent the tank.

semantic_claims.proposition: Valerius firmware 4.1.9 displays overpressure when the auxiliary tank exceeds 450 kPa.
The overpressure state means the panel freezes the last validated flow rate and does not mean the main valve has failed.
If overpressure persists for 5 minutes, engineers should inspect the relief valve, and when bypass BYP-11 is active, they must not reset the module.
A reset of the module clears the overpressure display but does not vent the tank.
These overpressure display and reset characteristics apply to Valerius firmware 4.1.9 starting from 2041-02-18.

fixtures.source: In the Ciphera repository, `glyph` refers to raw sensor inputs, and `sigil` refers to processed classifications. `NodeGate` reads `glyph` from `/var/ciphera/in/node.glf` via `data.input_path`. It writes `sigil` to `/var/ciphera/out/node.sig` via `data.output_path`. For input specs, see [glyph spec](https://doc.ciphera.invalid/glyph) and select **Raw Glyph**. For output specs, see [sigil spec](https://doc.ciphera.invalid/sigil) and select **Processed Sigil**. Preserve error `ERR_GLYPH expected glyph got sigil`.

semantic_claims.proposition: In the Ciphera repository, glyph refers to raw sensor inputs and sigil refers to processed classifications.
NodeGate reads glyph and writes sigil.
Input specifications are at https://doc.ciphera.invalid/glyph and output specifications are at https://doc.ciphera.invalid/sigil.
NodeGate reads glyph from /var/ciphera/in/node.glf via data.input_path and writes sigil to /var/ciphera/out/node.sig via data.output_path.
Users must select Raw Glyph for input specifications and Processed Sigil for output specifications.
The system preserves the error code ERR_GLYPH expected glyph got sigil.

fixtures.source: This wipes memory on idle buoy `T-10`. It does not affect active buoy `T-12`. Confirm that permit `WIPE-44` is valid, `T-10` is disconnected, and the console shows **Safe to Purge**. Run `thalassactl buoy check T-10`. Proceed only if it returns `status=idle mem=full`. WARNING: The next command permanently deletes all data on `T-10`. A remote restore is impossible. Run `thalassactl buoy purge T-10 --permit WIPE-44`. Run `thalassactl buoy verify T-10` and confirm it returns `mem=empty`.

semantic_claims.proposition: The memory wipe procedure affects idle buoy T-10 but does not affect active buoy T-12.
Before purge execution, confirm permit WIPE-44 is valid, buoy T-10 is disconnected, the console displays Safe to Purge, and thalassactl buoy check T-10 returns status=idle mem=full.
The purge command permanently deletes all data on buoy T-10 and a remote restore is impossible.
After the purge, running thalassactl buoy verify T-10 must return mem=empty.
